name: United States Tennis Association
summary: The national governing body for tennis in the United States. It traces its roots to 1881, owns and runs the US Open, and manages American participation in the Davis Cup and Billie Jean King Cup.

founded.text: 1881, as the U.S. National Lawn Tennis Association

headquarters.editorNote: Not verified: the USTA contact page lists offices in Westchester County (Purchase, NY), New York City and Orlando but does not name one as headquarters; checked 2026-10-24.

name: Lawn Tennis Association
summary: The national governing body for tennis in Great Britain, the Channel Islands and the Isle of Man, founded in 1888. Since November 2020 it has also been the recognised governing body for padel.

headquarters.text: 100 Priory Lane, Roehampton, London, United Kingdom
headquarters.citation: Clause 1.1, address of LTA Operations Limited

name: Fédération française de tennis
summary: France's national tennis federation, which also governs padel, beach tennis, pickleball, para tennis and courte paume (real tennis) and runs Roland-Garros. It began in 1888 as a lawn tennis commission and took its current name in 1976.

founded.text: 1888, as the Commission de Lawn Tennis of the USFSA; Fédération française de lawn tennis from 1920

nameChange.text: Became the Fédération française de lawn tennis in 1920 and dropped 'lawn' to take its current name in 1976

name: Deutscher Tennis Bund
summary: Germany's national tennis federation, based at the Rothenbaum stadium in Hamburg. Working with 17 regional member associations, it describes itself as the largest tennis federation in the world, with about 1.4 million members in nearly 9,000 clubs.

founded.text: 19 May 1902 in Berlin, as the Deutscher Lawn Tennis Bund; re-founded as the Deutscher Tennis Bund after the Second World War

members.text: About 1.4 million members in almost 9,000 clubs, through 17 regional associations

nameChange.text: Founded as the Deutscher Lawn Tennis Bund in 1902; re-founded under the name Deutscher Tennis Bund the year after the 1948 German championships

name: Real Federación Española de Tenis
summary: Spain's national tennis federation, based in Barcelona. It was founded in San Sebastián in 1909 and took its current royal name in 1957.

founded.text: 11 September 1909 in San Sebastián, as the Asociación General de Lawn Tennis

headquarters.text: Gran Via de Carles III 124, Barcelona, Spain

formerNames: Asociación de Lawn Tennis de España

nameChange.text: Dropped its royal title in 1931, took the name Federación Española de Tenis at the end of 1935, and regained the royal title as the Real Federación Española de Tenis in 1957

name: Japan Tennis Association
summary: Japan's national tennis federation, based in Tokyo. It grew out of a tennis association formed in 1922 and became a public-interest foundation in 2012.

founded.text: 1922, as its predecessor the Nihon Teikyū Kyōkai (日本庭球協会); reorganised as the Japan Tennis Association foundation in 1980
founded.citation: 日本テニス協会の歴史

headquarters.text: Japan Sport Olympic Square, Shinjuku, Tokyo, Japan
headquarters.citation: Address on the About the JTA page

formerNames: Nihon Teikyū Kyōkai (日本庭球協会)

name: Tennis Canada
summary: Canada's national sport association for tennis, founded in 1890. It owns and runs the National Bank Open (the ATP and WTA events in Montreal and Toronto) and is a member of World Tennis (the ITF).

name: Federazione Italiana Tennis e Padel
summary: Italy's national federation for tennis, padel and beach tennis (with pickleball as an experimental discipline), based in Rome. Founded in Florence in 1910, it was the Federazione Italiana Tennis (FIT) until it added padel to its name from 1 January 2023.

founded.text: 16 May 1910 in Florence, as the Federazione italiana di lawn-tennis

nameChange.text: Renamed from Federazione Italiana Tennis (FIT) to Federazione Italiana Tennis e Padel (FITP) by the national assembly on 16 October 2022, in use from 1 January 2023
